result.topic_en: Notes on Abelian integrals: representing G(x,y)/f'(x,y) as a linear combination of the integrands φ_α of the first kind, a bilinear relation for the derivatives of the fundamental function φ(x,y,ξ,η) in terms of φ_α and second-kind integrands ψ_α, and notation for the corresponding integrals ω_α, ϖ_α, Ω.
result.transcription:
Coefficienten, so dass man
$\frac{G(x,y)}{f'(x,y)} = C_1 \varphi_1(x,y) + \cdots + C_\rho \varphi_\rho(x,y)$
setzen kann.
Die Schlussfolgerung[?] hat man stets[?]
$\frac{\partial}{\partial \xi} \varphi(x,y,\xi,\eta) - \frac{\partial}{\partial x} \varphi(\xi,\eta,x,y)$
$= \sum \{ \varphi_\alpha(x,y)\psi(\xi,\eta)_\alpha - \varphi_\alpha(\xi,\eta)\psi_\alpha(x,y) \}$
wo $\psi_1(x,y), \ldots, \psi_\rho(x,y)$ rationale Functionen
von $x,y$ ebenfalls von der Form
$\frac{G(x,y)}{f'(x,y)}$
sind, welche ebenfalls die Eigenschaft haben,
dass in den Entwicklungen derselben
nach steigenden Potenzen von $x-x_0$
die Anfangsglieder stets vom Exponenten[?]
von dem $(-1)$ten Grade[?] sind.
Es werden nun
$\int \varphi_\alpha(x,y)\,dx = \omega(x,y)_\alpha$
$\int \psi_\alpha(x,y)\,dx = \varpi(x,y)_\alpha$
$\int \varphi(x,y,\xi,\eta)\,dx = \Omega(x,y,\xi,\eta)$

methods.what: Expression of G/f' as linear combination of the ρ integrands of the first kind
Bilinear (exchange) relation for the fundamental function φ(x,y,ξ,η) in terms of first- and second-kind integrands
Definition of Abelian integrals of first kind, second kind, and the integral of the fundamental function
